defects.title: open_cube_store's ALPHACUBE_DAILY_FIELDS fallback makes the build script crash before it does anything — the script that creates the daily store refuses to run because the daily store does not exist yet
defects.failure_scenario: main() calls open_cube_store(str(store_dir)) with no daily_root, and open_cube_store (src/alphacube/store.py:444-445) does `if daily_root is None: daily_root = os.environ.get("ALPHACUBE_DAILY_FIELDS")`. That env var is the design's documented way to point AlphaCube at the daily store, so on the server it will most naturally be set to exactly the --out default (/root/autodl-tmp/AlphaCube/daily_fields). On the FIRST build that directory does not exist, so CubeStore.__init__ (store.py:131) does DailyFieldStore(daily_root) and the script dies with an uncaught FileNotFoundError: <out>/meta.json, before the schema probe, the side-by-side symbol print or anything else. Reproduced: /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP9/attack_env.py sets os.environ['ALPHACUBE_DAILY_FIELDS'] = str(out) and then calls bdf.main([...]) on a synthetic store -> FileNotFoundError at store.py:131 / dailyfields.py:281, traceback, no diagnostics. Same env var also makes the delivered tests environment-dependent: `ALPHACUBE_DAILY_FIELDS=/tmp/does_not_exist_daily ~/.venvs/alphacube/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_build_daily_fields.py -q` -> 12 failed, 10 passed (all 14 tests that go through main()). Secondary effect when the env var points at an EXISTING stale store: the script silently attaches it and sha256s its meta.json, which contradicts the design's 'opens the cube store read-only purely for its canonical symbols/dates'.
defects.suggested_fix:
Neutralise the env fallback at the one call site. Either pop/restore it around the open:

    saved = os.environ.pop("ALPHACUBE_DAILY_FIELDS", None)
    try:
        store = open_cube_store(str(store_dir))
    finally:
        if saved is not None:
            os.environ["ALPHACUBE_DAILY_FIELDS"] = saved

or dispatch directly the way open_cube_store does (SegmentedCubeStore(p) when (p/'minute'/META_FILE).is_file() else CubeStore(p)), which also documents 'no daily source is attached while we build one'. Add a regression test with monkeypatch.setenv("ALPHACUBE_DAILY_FIELDS", str(tmp_path / "not_built_yet")) around the happy-path build.

defects.title: A date file whose schema is short of read_cols crashes mid-build with a raw ArrowInvalid that does not name the file
defects.failure_scenario: build_planes does pd.read_parquet(path, columns=read_cols) for every store date, with read_cols fixed from the ONE probed file. In a years-long vendor directory a column can appear or disappear partway through the history. Reproduced (attack_misc.py case A2): a cap-dir where only the first date carries circulating_shares -> the probe sees it, FloatShares is scheduled, and the second date's read raises `pyarrow.lib.ArrowInvalid: No match for FieldRef.Name(circulating_shares) in symbol: large_string`. The message names neither the date nor the path, the traceback is raw pyarrow, and the whole build (minutes of parquet reads at server scale) is lost. The same happens for a corrupt/truncated parquet or a later file missing total_market_value.
defects.suggested_fix: Wrap the per-date read: `try: df = pd.read_parquet(path, columns=read_cols) except Exception as e: raise SystemExit(f"{path}: cannot read columns {read_cols} ({e}); the schema probed at {sample_path} does not hold for every date") from e`, or (friendlier for an optional field) read the file's schema with pyarrow.parquet.read_schema, skip the columns it lacks, count those dates per field and print the count next to the coverage line so the hole is visible instead of fatal.

defects.title: The published --out directory inherits mkdtemp's 0700 mode, so a reader running as another user cannot open the daily store
defects.failure_scenario: tempfile.mkdtemp always creates the directory with mode 0700, and os.replace carries that mode onto --out. Measured (attack_misc.py case A6): the built daily_fields directory comes out 0o700 while the cube store that write_synthetic_store/build_cube_store produces next to it is 0o755. Any process not running as the building user (a different service account, a mining job under another user, an operator inspecting the files) gets PermissionError on <out>/meta.json, which surfaces downstream as 'daily_root cannot be opened' rather than as a permissions problem.
defects.suggested_fix: Before the rename, give the temp directory the mode a normal mkdir would get: `os.chmod(tmp, 0o777 & ~_umask())` (read the umask with os.umask(0) / os.umask(old)), or simply os.chmod(tmp, 0o755) to match build_cube_store's output. Assert the resulting mode in the primary test.

defects.title: The rebuild refusal fires only after the entire build, instead of as a cheap path check at the start
defects.failure_scenario: The 'out already exists non-empty' refusal lives inside write_daily_field_store, i.e. after the store open, the probe, every parquet read and the coverage gate. Reproduced end-to-end (attack_rerun.py): run1 rc=0, run2 raises SystemExit('could not move the newly built directory into place ... remove it first and re-run'); the old directory is intact and no temp dir leaks, so nothing is damaged, but on the real server the operator pays a full multi-minute build to learn a fact that is knowable from a single stat() call. This is the one place the implementation extends the design's literal step 7, and it is the step an operator hits on every second run (e.g. after adding the real share-column name).
defects.suggested_fix: Add the check to main() right next to refuse_if_out_inside_sources: `if out_dir.exists() and any(out_dir.iterdir()): raise SystemExit(f"{out_dir} already exists and is not empty; remove it first (this script never overwrites a previous build)")` — keeping the late check in write_daily_field_store as the belt-and-braces guard. If rebuilds should instead just work, do the swap atomically: os.replace(tmp, out_dir) when out_dir is absent/empty, else os.replace(out_dir, out_dir.with_name(out_dir.name + ".old")) then os.replace(tmp, out_dir) then rmtree the .old.

defects.title: The test suite does not pin summarize's 'first/last date with any data': always returning the whole date axis stays green
defects.failure_scenario: Mutation (harness /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP9/mutate.py, case M8): replacing summarize's `date_range[name] = (dates[int(has_data[0])], dates[int(has_data[-1])])` with `(dates[0], dates[-1])` leaves tests/test_build_daily_fields.py at 22 passed. The only date_range assertion is `meta["date_range"][name] == [dates[0], dates[2]]` in the primary test, and that fixture has data on date 0 and date 2 of a 3-date axis -- exactly the axis ends -- so the assertion cannot tell 'first/last date with any data' (design step 7) from 'the whole range'. A real build whose cap-dir starts later than the store's day axis would report a misleading date_range and nothing would catch it. (8 of the 10 mutations I tried were killed, so this is a gap, not a pattern.)
defects.suggested_fix: Make the fixture's data span differ from the axis: add a 4th store date with no parquet at all (or drop date 0's file and keep dates 1-2), so the expected date_range is a strict sub-range, and assert it per field -- e.g. build FloatShares only on the middle date and assert date_range['FloatShares'] == [dates[1], dates[1]] while FloatCap's stays wider.

defects.title: The test suite does not pin the atomic publish: replacing os.replace with shutil.copytree stays green
defects.failure_scenario: Mutation (mutate.py case M10): replacing `os.replace(tmp, out_dir)` with `shutil.copytree(tmp, out_dir)` leaves tests/test_build_daily_fields.py at 22 passed, although it breaks design step 7 outright -- the publish is no longer atomic (a crash during the copy leaves a half-written, DailyFieldStore-openable --out) and every successful run leaves a `.daily_fields.<rand>.tmp` directory behind beside --out forever. test_an_interrupted_write_leaves_nothing_a_daily_field_store_will_open only interrupts inside np.save, i.e. strictly before the rename, so it cannot see this; and no test looks for leftovers after a SUCCESSFUL build.
defects.suggested_fix: Two cheap assertions: (1) in the primary build test, after rc == 0 assert `[p for p in out.parent.glob(f".{out.name}.*")] == []`; (2) add a test that monkeypatches bdf.os.replace to raise OSError and asserts SystemExit, `not out.exists()` and no leftover temp directory -- which pins that the final step is a rename of a fully written directory rather than a per-file copy into --out.

result.notes:
范围与环境核对
- 只碰了清单内的两个文件:git show --name-only cab4312 = scripts/build_daily_fields.py, tests/test_build_daily_fields.py。worktree 干净(git status --porcelain 空),分支 partura-steering。
- 向后兼容/随机数流:确实不适用。grep 'build_daily_fields' 全仓只在 src/alphacube/dailyfields.py:40/168 的 docstring 里出现,没有任何代码 import 这个脚本;两个文件都是新增,不触碰 TypedTreeGenerator/GPMiner 等任何消耗 self._rng 的路径,没有新分支会在默认参数下被进入。整套测试 831 passed / 10 skipped / 1 xfailed / 0 failed(基线 617 是 WP1 之前的数,WP1–WP5 已并入本分支,WP9 自己贡献 22 个,单跑 tests/test_build_daily_fields.py 得 22 passed)。
- 设计 WP9 的 9 个 step 全部实现,CLI 名称与默认值逐字对上(--store 必填;--cap-dir=/root/autodl-tmp/qmt_daily_data/daily_capital;--out=/root/autodl-tmp/AlphaCube/daily_fields;--only 可重复;--min-coverage=0.5;--dry-run)。step 3 的「两边各前 10 个 symbol 并排打印」既在正常流程里打,也重复进了覆盖率失败的消息里;step 6 的「只在真有 share 列时才写 FloatShares、绝不由 FloatCap/Close 合成」「不写任何 Log* 面」都做到了;step 7 的 meta.json 是 DailyFieldStore.__init__ 所读键的严格超集;step 9 的 derived/log 提示在 dry-run 下也打。

我验证过、确认没问题的点(攻击脚本在 /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP9/,未改动 worktree 任何已跟踪文件)
- 对齐与 NaN 位置:行用 store 的 symbol 顺序、列用 store 的 date 顺序,缺文件/缺 symbol 都是 NaN;镜像了 tearsheet.load_caps 的 .map + 布尔掩码写法,索引没有错位(M1 变异立刻被测死)。
- parquet 的 symbol 列被 pyarrow 读回成 category dtype(字典编码,生产上很常见)时 .map(row_of) 仍然正确(attack_misc A4)。
- 同一天出现重复 symbol 行时取最后一行(A3:1.0/7.0 两行 -> 7.0),不会报错也不会污染别的行;vendor 快照一般不该有重复,先只记一笔。
- --out 是指向 --cap-dir 内部的 symlink 也会被拒(A7,resolve() 先解符号链接);--out 只是源目录的兄弟目录则不会被误拒(测试里有非空性守卫)。
- --out 已存在但为空目录时 os.replace 正常成功(A5),不会误报。
- 失败路径不留垃圾:np.save 中途炸、os.replace 失败,两种情况 tmp 目录都被 rmtree,--out 原样不动(A3/attack_rerun 均确认 leftover 为空)。
- 变异测试 10 个里 8 个被测死(值被改、覆盖率闸门失效、tmp 不清理、refuse 变空操作、写 float32、缺文件当 0、去掉 require_board_rule、失败消息里去掉 symbol 样本),说明这套测试总体是真的;只有 date_range 与原子 rename 两条没被钉住(已作为 defect 列出)。

对实现者几条 deviation 的裁定
- require_board_rule(store.symbols) 的追加:同意保留。dailyfields.py 自己的 docstring 把本脚本列为仅两处必需调用点之一,而本脚本开 store 时没有 daily_root,CubeStore/SegmentedCubeStore 内置的那次 attach 检查不会触发,所以不显式调一次确实会漏。唯一的小瑕疵是它排在 schema 探测与并排 symbol 打印之前,于是 SH.600000 这类拼写的 store 只会看到「no board rule can ever fire」,看不到最能解释问题的两行 symbol 对比;建议把这次调用挪到覆盖率闸门旁边(docstring 原话就是 "next to its coverage floor"),或者先打印再检查。另外注意这条检查会让一个纯主板 store 连 FloatCap/TotalCap 都建不出来——但 CubeStore 的 daily attach 本来也会拒,行为是一致的,不算缺陷。
- 「os.replace 不能覆盖非空目录,所以大声失败而不是 shutil.rmtree」:方向同意(绝不该偷偷删旧目录),但位置应该提前,见 defect 4。
- SHARE_COLUMN_CANDIDATES 猜列名:接受这个处理方式(猜不中就不写 FloatShares,下游 resolve 会明确报错,是正确的失败模式)。但比改源码里的 tuple 更好的办法是加一个 --share-column NAME 开关:操作员第一次在服务器上看到打印出来的 `columns: [...]` 就能直接用上,不必编辑文件;顺便建议在覆盖率那几行旁边再打每个字段的 median/min/max,因为猜中列名但单位不对(例如「万股」)是这里唯一会静默产生错数据的风险,而量级一眼就能看出来。
- 英文注释、--dry-run 的语义(跑完全部校验与内存构建、只跳过落盘)、probe_schema 没有日期命中时退回目录里最早的文件:都合理,无异议。
- 「--min-coverage 默认 0.5」是设计钉死的参数,不是实现问题;但提醒一句:coverage 是在整个 (S, D) 矩形上算的,包含大量「该股当时还没上市」的格子,真实全市场跑下来很可能接近甚至低于 0.5,第一次上服务器大概率需要显式传 --min-coverage,而失败消息现在断言「几乎总是 symbol 格式不匹配」,可能误导。建议消息里同时给出「或者你的日期轴远早于 cap-dir 的起始日期」这一可能,或者把覆盖率同时按「有任何数据的日期范围内」再算一个数一起打印。
- 另外两点非缺陷的观察:source 列里值为 0 的市值会被当作有效值写进去(符合 step 5 的字面要求),到 resolve 里 log(0) 会变成 -inf 而不是 NaN——这是已并入的 dailyfields.resolve 的地盘,不在 WP9 改,但值得在服务器首跑时看一眼有没有 0;argparse 的 description 用了 __doc__.splitlines()[0],在 python -OO 下会 AttributeError,无实际影响。
